issues.description: Memory conformity is generated by a dyadic interaction in which the two partners mutually influence each other, so the two members of a pair produce non-independent data. Randomization is explicitly done at the pair level ('Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned'), yet the power analysis and planned ANOVAs treat the 240 individuals as independent observations. This clustering inflates the effective degrees of freedom and Type I error rate, and means the reported required sample sizes (computed on individual N) are wrong. The analysis plan does not mention any multilevel/clustered approach to handle the pair structure.
issues.quote: The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs).

issues.subcategory: underpowered for the plausible effect size
issues.description: The authors themselves note that the prior interventions most similar to theirs (warning, reinforced self-affirmation, cognitive interview) produced inconsistent or null effects on memory conformity, implying the true effect of reduction techniques is most likely small. Yet the chosen sample (240) provides power only for medium and large effects, not small ones. The study is therefore likely underpowered for the most realistic effect size, risking an uninformative null.
issues.quote: Considering the accessible financial, organizational and time resources, a sample of 240 participants was assumed; this allows for excellent power to detect medium and large effect sizes but not small ones.

issues.description: The two studies used to derive the replication effect size differ enormously (Hedges' g = 1.92 vs g = 0.38), indicating very high heterogeneity. Pooling them into a single random-effects estimate of 1.13 to justify a required N of 18 is statistically problematic; the pooled value is not a meaningful population estimate when the inputs are this discrepant, and the resulting power claim is unreliable.
issues.quote: Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13.

issues.subcategory: effect-size source does not match planned measure
issues.description: The power/effect-size estimates are taken from prior studies (Ito et al., 2019; Kękuś et al., 2020) that used two-alternative forced-choice individual memory tests, but the present study deliberately switches to open-ended questions. The authors acknowledge this change yet still use the forced-choice-based effect sizes and the same low repeated-measures correlation (0.07) to plan power, even though open-ended scoring will yield a different distribution of correct/misled/other responses and different effect magnitudes.
issues.quote: First we will examine the memory conformity effect using the procedure of Garry et al. (2008; also Ito et al., 2019), but with modification concerning applying open-ended questions in the individual memory test.

issues.description: The three experimental conditions are not equated for format, duration, or active engagement, so any differences cannot be attributed to content. The Extended warning and Education conditions are ~7-minute passive podcasts, but the Demonstration-and-motivation condition adds an active DRM task with personalized feedback plus a podcast, and the control condition is an unrelated soft-skills podcast of unspecified length. Differences in time-on-task, active vs passive processing, and personalized feedback are confounded with the manipulated content—particularly threatening the prediction that Demonstration-and-motivation will be most effective.
issues.quote: the motivational aspect will be achieved by a podcast (i.e., only with sound; no visual material will be included) explaining how harmful a situation is in which one witness reports details that they do not actually remember but which were heard from other witnesses.

issues.description: The experimenter administers the condition-specific podcasts and personally delivers the DRM feedback and motivational encouragement, and later collects responses and judges whether participants 'guessed' the hypothesis. No blinding of the experimenter to condition, and no standardization safeguards against experimenter expectancy effects, are described. This is especially problematic given the subjective exclusion decision (guessing hypotheses) and the directional predictions.
issues.quote: the experimenter will give the following information to the participants: “Thank you for completing this memory task. Please take a look at your sheets now.

issues.description: Participants who 'correctly guess' the hypotheses are excluded and replaced, and the authors acknowledge this will likely occur more often in the experimental groups than the control group. Replacing excluded participants to maintain N, combined with differential exclusion rates across conditions and a subjective criterion for 'guessing,' introduces selection bias and a researcher degree of freedom that could systematically bias the between-group comparison.
issues.quote: If any of the participants correctly guesses our hypotheses, they will be excluded from the analysis and replaced with another person in order to maintain the correct sample size. We realize that this may result in more exclusion in the three experimental groups than in the control group

issues.subcategory: undisclosed prior data / selection of stimuli for strongest effect
issues.description: The DRM lists are to be chosen on the basis of unreported 'previous research' specifically because they 'produce the strongest effect.' Selecting stimuli to maximize an effect based on undocumented prior data is a researcher degree of freedom that is not pre-specified or referenced, undermining reproducibility and inflating the demonstrated 'vulnerability.'
issues.quote: Four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect.

issues.subcategory: DRM false memory mismatched to misinformation/source monitoring
issues.description: The DRM paradigm produces associative/gist-based false memories, a mechanism widely argued to be distinct from the source-monitoring and social-influence processes underlying eyewitness misinformation/memory conformity. Using DRM both to 'demonstrate' relevant vulnerability and as a predictor of MORI conformity assumes a shared mechanism that is theoretically contested, creating a construct-validity mismatch.
issues.quote: The demonstration of the fallibility of memory will be done by means of the DRM technique (see detailed description below)

issues.description: A central moderation hypothesis is that the techniques work mainly for participants 'aware of the discrepancies.' However, the only related coding described is the behaviorally derived 'disputed' vs 'non-disputed' classification during discussion, which is not the same construct as a participant remembering both the original and the co-witness detail at test. The manuscript does not specify how awareness of discrepancies will actually be measured, leaving the key moderator untestable as stated.
issues.quote: Thus, we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies.

issues.description: The 'disputed' vs 'non-disputed' classification is determined by participants' own behavior during discussion rather than by random assignment, so comparisons across these categories are confounded with self-selection (e.g., more confident or better-encoding participants may dispute more). This is presented as an analysis but its non-random nature and potential confounds are not addressed, and subgroup sizes/power are not specified.
issues.quote: we will categorize participants’ answers into two groups: “disputed” and “non-disputed”.

issues.subcategory: multiple non-independent dependent variables without correction
issues.description: The plan is to run ANOVAs on four indices (correct, misinformation-consistent, other, total answers), which are mathematically interdependent (the first three are constrained by the total). Running separate ANOVAs on these interlocking indices inflates Type I error and risks contradictory/redundant inferences; no correction for multiplicity or rationale for treating them separately is provided.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers.

issues.subcategory: collected measure with no analysis plan
issues.description: Participants rate subjective certainty (0–100%) for every answer, but no hypothesis or analysis involving confidence is specified. Collecting a measure without a pre-specified analysis creates an undisclosed researcher degree of freedom (it could be analyzed selectively later) and is a reporting gap for a Registered Report.
issues.quote: Moreover, for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% (complete uncertainty, guessing) to 100% (absolute certainty).

issues.description: The control podcast topic ('soft skills related to social attitudes') and its duration are not specified, preventing evaluation of whether it matches the experimental conditions in length and engagement. Without this information, the adequacy of the control condition and the equating of conditions cannot be assessed or replicated.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.description: The sample is a self-selected, media-recruited Polish convenience sample restricted to ages 16–35, yet the study draws conclusions intended for 'the proper functioning of justice systems' and real eyewitnesses, who span a far wider age range and include populations (e.g., older adults) known to differ in suggestibility. The narrow age band and convenience recruitment limit generalizability to actual forensic contexts, a limitation not acknowledged.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.

issues.description: There are only eight critical details, split into four discussed and four non-discussed per pair. Estimating per-condition accuracy from as few as four items yields coarse, low-reliability measures with restricted variance, which weakens the sensitivity of the within-subjects conformity comparison and the moderation analyses. This measurement limitation is not discussed.
issues.quote: The test will comprise 12 questions, four of which refer to critical details (e.g., What color was Eric’s cap?), with the other eight being control questions.

issues.subcategory: directional hypotheses tested with non-directional tests
issues.description: The authors make explicit ordinal predictions about relative efficacy (Demonstration-and-motivation > Extended warning > Education) but state that 'non-directional significance tests are assumed.' The mismatch between directional theoretical predictions and the planned omnibus/non-directional comparisons leaves the ordering hypothesis without a specified confirmatory test (e.g., a planned contrast/trend test).
issues.quote: Comparisons among all groups and non-directional significance tests are assumed.

issues.description: The predicted ranking of technique effectiveness is described as merely 'tentative' and is grounded largely in a single persuasion study (Sagarin et al., 2002) from a different domain, plus the inconsistent warning literature. Given that the conditions are confounded (see format/dose issue), this prediction is not well-grounded theoretically and cannot be cleanly tested.
issues.quote: Based on the research of Sagarin et al. (2002), we tentatively assume that the most effective technique in reducing the memory conformity effect will be Demonstration and motivation

issues.subcategory: acknowledged confound between mechanisms within techniques
issues.description: The authors concede substantial overlap between interventions (memory education appears in both Education and Demonstration-and-motivation), so even if effects emerge, the study cannot isolate which component or mechanism is responsible. This limits the causal/mechanistic conclusions the design can support.
issues.quote: we are aware of some overlap between the three interventions, for instance, teaching about memory is included is present in a way in both Education about memory and Demonstration and motivation.

issues.subcategory: inconsistent description of DRM lure feedback
issues.description: The Demonstration-and-motivation method is said to use 'Four lists' with one example list (critical lure 'doctor'), but the scripted feedback names four lures ('doctor, window, sweet, thief') without describing the corresponding three additional lists or their words. The materials description is therefore internally incomplete/inconsistent, preventing replication of the demonstration.
issues.quote: See if you have written down any of the words: doctor, window, sweet, thief.

issues.subcategory: exploratory predictor framed without mechanism control
issues.description: DRM performance is to be used as a 'possible predictor' of MORI conformity. Because the DRM task is itself part of one experimental manipulation and is only administered to that group, using DRM scores as a predictor of conformity conflates an individual-difference correlation with the manipulation, and any predictive relationship cannot support causal/mechanistic interpretation. The analysis is labeled exploratory but its interpretive limits are not stated.
issues.quote: As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique.

issues.description: When pairs cannot agree during collaborative recall, 'both responses will be documented,' but the scoring rule for how such dual responses feed into the misinformation-exposure classification and the individual-test indices is not fully specified. Similarly, how missing item-level responses ('don't know') are handled across the four indices and in the ANOVA is underspecified, leaving room for undisclosed analytic choices.
issues.quote: If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented.
